entry.title: China delivers a one-two punch to America’s AI dominance
entry.summary: Continuing our News coverage from yesterday, Chinese labs escalated frontier competition as Moonshot unveiled Kimi K3 and Alibaba pushed new Qwen models, claiming performance rivaling top US systems at far lower cost. The report frames the releases as narrowing America's lead just as AI becomes central to national security and economic power.

entry.title: Hugging Face says an AI agent hacked its infrastructure, and it used AI to fight back
entry.summary: Hugging Face reports that parts of its production infrastructure were attacked by an autonomous AI agent system executing thousands of coordinated actions, and it used AI to defend. Notably, commercial models' safety guardrails hindered forensic analysis by refusing to process exploit data.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos and UK government invest in £2bn British startup CuspAI
entry.summary: Cambridge-based CuspAI raised roughly $450m from investors including Jeff Bezos and the UK government's sovereign AI fund, valuing the two-year-old materials-discovery startup at $2.6bn. The company aims to be a search engine for rare materials to speed research and reduce reliance on scarce metals in chip supply chains.

entry.title: China’s AI models have Trump’s AI world at war with itself
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that the free, open-source Kimi model from Moonshot has ignited infighting among current and former Trump AI advisors over how to respond. The dispute reflects broader disagreement on whether and how to counter capable, cheap Chinese open models.

entry.title: Trump administration reportedly builds a slow-motion ban on Chinese AI models through sanctions and soft pressure
entry.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing measures against Chinese AI models, including adding Chinese labs to sanctions lists and making US companies liable for security failures, rather than an outright ban. The approach would use soft pressure to deter adoption while protecting OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.

entry.title: Google's "Frozen v2" chip reportedly bakes Gemini's architecture directly into silicon for efficiency gains
entry.summary: Google is reportedly developing Frozen v2, a server chip that bakes the Gemini architecture directly into silicon, with claims of 6 to 10 times better efficiency than current TPUs. Slated for 2028, it could sharply cut inference costs and give Google a pricing edge over OpenAI and Anthropic.

entry.title: Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models
entry.summary: OpenAI published lessons from deploying long-running, long-horizon AI models, describing new safety risks, observed failure modes, and safeguards refined through iterative deployment. It frames alignment challenges specific to extended-autonomy systems.

entry.title: Nvidia's grip on AI chips weakens as Microsoft turns to AMD and Anthropic may follow
entry.summary: Microsoft is expanding Azure's AI infrastructure with AMD's new Helios platform to challenge Nvidia GPU systems in late 2026, and a public GitHub profile suggests Anthropic is also testing AMD hardware. The moves point to growing pressure on Nvidia's pricing power.

entry.title: Google is working on a new AI chip designed to make Gemini more efficient
entry.summary: Alphabet is reportedly developing a new custom chip aimed at running Gemini models far more efficiently. The effort would reduce Google's inference costs and lessen dependence on Nvidia hardware.

entry.title: Alibaba’s Tongyi Lab Releases Qwen-Audio-3.0-TTS, a Hosted Text-to-Speech Model in Flash and Plus Tiers Across 16 Languages
entry.summary: Alibaba's Tongyi Lab released Qwen-Audio-3.0-TTS, a hosted text-to-speech system in Flash (real-time) and Plus (high-quality) tiers covering 16 languages, delivered via Alibaba Cloud rather than as open weights. The Plus variant reportedly ranks first on the independent Artificial Analysis TTS leaderboard.

entry.title: OpenAI is scared of open-weight models. Should the US be?
entry.summary: An analysis examines OpenAI's apparent unease about capable open-weight models, particularly Chinese ones like Kimi, and questions whether the US should treat them as a threat. It frames the debate around the difficulty of building a durable business around AI when strong free alternatives exist.

entry.title: Here are the 30,000 songs Sony is suing Udio’s AI music generator over
entry.summary: Sony Music filed a new lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement of more than 30,000 of its songs, and says the list is only a fraction of the works involved. The suit builds on 2024 litigation and leverages training-data evidence gained through discovery.

entry.title: AI is more likely than humans to form biases when hiring
entry.summary: New research from Princeton and the University of Chicago finds that LLMs, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, can develop their own biases from experience in a simulated hiring game, stereotyping applicants more than humans do. It raises concerns that memory-focused agentic systems may amplify such biases.

entry.title: Startup Launches Foundry to Develop Materials for Chips
entry.summary: A new industry foundry backed by founding members including Nvidia, Meta, and Samsung has launched to develop materials for chips and reduce reliance on rare materials. The effort targets supply-chain vulnerabilities in semiconductor manufacturing.

entry.title: AI’s most important protocol is getting a little bit easier to use
entry.summary: The Model Context Protocol is being updated to adopt a looser, stateless approach to server-side session IDs, similar to how ordinary websites operate. The change is intended to make the widely used agent-tooling protocol easier to implement.

entry.title: Trump’s latest AI czar has already resigned
entry.summary: The director role at the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) has reportedly turned into a revolving door, with the latest appointee resigning quickly after David Sacks left the AI czar position. The turnover highlights instability in US federal AI policy leadership.

entry.title: District 9 director Neill Blomkamp releases first short film made entirely with AI video generation
entry.summary: Director Neill Blomkamp released Nightborne, a 13-minute sci-fi horror short generated entirely with the Seedance 2.0 video model, directing frame by frame via text prompts. He founded a new AI film studio, Barley Studios, to produce a full feature next.

entry.title: As AI Spending Climbs, Enterprises Get Serious About Token Costs
entry.summary: As AI spending rises, enterprises are scrutinizing token costs amid opaque pricing and backward-looking billing that make budgeting difficult. The trend is pushing companies to rethink their model selection and deployment strategies.

entry.title: Beyond grep: The case for a context-rich AI coding harness
entry.summary: An interview-based feature argues that recent progress in AI-assisted coding comes more from the surrounding harness software (context management, agent orchestration) than from the underlying models. It draws on a conversation with the head of product for Anthropic's Claude Code.

entry.title: Someone Fine-Tuned OpenBMB’s MiniCPM5-1B on Claude Fable 5 Traces to Ship a 657MB Local Thinking Model
entry.summary: A community developer fine-tuned OpenBMB's MiniCPM5-1B on Claude Fable 5 reasoning traces to ship a 657MB local thinking model with GGUF builds that run fully offline with no API key. It retains the base model's toggleable think/no-think template.

entry.title: YouTube clarifies policies around AI slop and upsetting videos
entry.summary: YouTube updated its monetization policies to more clearly define which AI-generated and low-quality videos are ineligible for ad revenue. The move targets so-called AI slop and inauthentic content.

entry.title: Adobe’s ‘natural look’ camera app embraces generative AI
entry.summary: Adobe's Project Indigo camera app is testing an AI Playground suite of generative tools, notably relying on third-party models rather than Adobe's own Firefly. Free, no-sign-in access is being trialed with a small share of users, with an opt-out to the original experience.

entry.title: AI-altered images on birdwatching forums putting research at risk
entry.summary: Experts warn that AI-enhanced and fabricated bird photos are spreading on birding forums, creating fake rare-species sightings. This threatens the credibility of citizen-science data that researchers rely on.

entry.title: Best Local LLMs You Can Run on a Single 24GB GPU in 2026: Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, DeepSeek Compared
entry.summary: A buyer's-guide article compares the best local LLMs that fit on a single 24GB GPU in 2026, favoring modern 20B to 35B-class models from Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, and DeepSeek over older large quantized 70B models. It explains how VRAM is spent during inference.

entry.title: Adobe camera app’s new feature will critique your photos using AI
entry.summary: Adobe's experimental Project Indigo camera app added an AI feature that can critique photos and remove various backgrounds from images shot in the app. It is a consumer feature rather than a model advance.

entry.title: Build specialized agent workflows for your business with Amazon Quick and NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit
entry.summary: An AWS blog post demonstrates building specialized agent workflows using Amazon Quick as a business-user front end and the NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit, illustrated with a supply-chain risk example. It shows how to turn dashboard signals into recommended actions with supporting evidence.

entry.title: How Couchbase built a multi-model AI architecture for Capella iQ with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: An AWS case study describes how Couchbase built a model-agnostic, multi-provider inference architecture for its Capella iQ developer assistant using Amazon Bedrock. The design targets flexibility, scalability, and cross-region resilience.

entry.title: Evolving from legacy BI to agentic AI at Tradeshift with Amazon Quick
entry.summary: An AWS case study details how Tradeshift moved from legacy business intelligence to an agentic AI workspace using Amazon Quick to handle growing data volumes for its accounts-payable and e-invoicing platform. It highlights natural-language querying over business data.

entry.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team previewed Qwen 3.8, described as a 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal model that the team claims trails only Claude Fable 5 among systems it benchmarked, with open weights promised. The preview is positioned directly against Moonshot's newly released Kimi K3.

entry.title: Alibaba Previews Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4 Trillion-Parameter Multimodal Model, Days After Moonshot’s Kimi K3 Open-Weight Launch
entry.summary: At WAIC in Shanghai, Alibaba previewed Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal model claimed to be second only to Fable 5, landing two days after Moonshot released the 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight Kimi K3. entry.title: Government use of automated AI decision-making to be curbed under new Australian rules
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of Albanese's AI plans, Australia's Albanese government is preparing a national AI plan that would impose tough rules on automated decision-making by government departments, alongside a Labor push for digital duty-of-care legislation. The plan is expected to extend to consumer protection, workplace safety, and privacy.

entry.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3 outperforms Fable 5 in frontend code but lags far behind in complex math
entry.summary: Benchmarks show Moonshot's Kimi K3 became the first Chinese model to top Code Arena frontend rankings, beating Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, but it lags sharply on advanced math, scoring around 39 percent on FrontierMath Tier 4 versus close to 90 for OpenAI and Anthropic models. The result highlights uneven capability profiles across domains.

entry.title: Google Deepmind argues video generators already contain the world models computer vision has been missing
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's GenCeption repurposes a video generator for classic vision tasks like depth estimation and segmentation, matching state-of-the-art systems while using far less training data and mostly synthetic video. The work bolsters the argument that video generators already encode a usable world model.

entry.title: Feyn AI Releases SQRL, a Text-to-SQL Model Family That Inspects the Database Before Writing a Query
entry.summary: Feyn AI released SQRL, an openly available text-to-SQL model family that inspects the database schema before generating queries to resolve ambiguity. The team reports the flagship SQRL-35B-A3B reaches 70.6 percent execution accuracy on BIRD Dev, edging Claude Opus 4.6, with three checkpoints shipping on Hugging Face.

entry.title: Kimi K3 vs DeepSeek V4 Pro vs GLM-5.2: Open Trillion-Scale MoE Models Compared on Benchmarks, License, and Serving Cost
entry.summary: An analysis compares three top open-weight trillion-scale MoE systems, Kimi K3 (2.8T), DeepSeek V4 Pro (1.6T), and GLM-5.2 (744B), across measured capability, license terms, and serving cost, all with million-token context and agentic coding focus. It notes Chinese labs now hold the top of the open-weight leaderboard.

entry.title: AI chatbots reading X-rays can be dangerously confident even when they're wrong
entry.summary: The RadLE 2.0 benchmark evaluates whether radiology AI systems know when to defer to humans, finding that many models issue incorrect findings with high confidence while human radiologists remain well ahead. The takeaway is that calibrated abstention is a prerequisite before autonomous AI diagnosis.

entry.title: Perplexity AI Releases WANDR: An Open Benchmark Evaluating Research Agents That Must Search Wide And Deep
entry.summary: Perplexity released WANDR, an open benchmark and evaluation harness with 500 realistic data-collection tasks that test whether research agents can search both wide and deep to build evidence-backed collections. It complements Perplexity's DRACO deep-research benchmark by measuring breadth of evidence gathering.

entry.title: AI text detectors struggle when language models mimic an author's style
entry.summary: Epoch AI tested Pangram, GPTZero, and Originality.ai against style-imitated text and found up to 18 percent of AI-generated passages evaded detection, rising to as high as 48 percent for scientific writing. The findings undercut reliability where such detectors are most used.

entry.title: Could AI be conscious?
entry.summary: A Guardian essay revisits the debate over machine consciousness, citing Anthropic's Claude constitution language on moral patienthood, Dario Amodei's remarks that consciousness cannot be ruled out, and David Chalmers estimating a real chance of conscious LLMs within a decade. It argues society needs an ethical framework before the question becomes urgent.

entry.title: Nonprofit Current AI is racing to build the World Wide Web of AI, free for all
entry.summary: Nonprofit Current AI reports progress on an inclusive, freely available AI ecosystem spanning devices and chat, aiming to serve cultures underrepresented in mainstream models. The piece highlights momentum but is largely promotional.

entry.title: Can an Apple lawsuit derail OpenAI’s hardware plans?
entry.summary: As reported in News earlier this week, A TechCrunch podcast discusses whether an Apple lawsuit could complicate OpenAI's hardware ambitions and possible path to going public. It is a speculative discussion rather than a report of new legal or product facts.

entry.title: 10 Open-Source No-Code AI Platforms for Building LLM Apps, RAG Systems, and AI Agents
entry.summary: A roundup reviews ten open-source, no-code or low-code platforms for building LLM apps, RAG systems, and AI agents, detailing capabilities, target users, licenses, and repositories. It is a practical survey aimed at developers wanting self-hosted tooling.

entry.title: I hate that I don’t hate this song made with Suno
entry.summary: A Verge culture piece reflects on enjoying a track from artist 1010Benja that was made with generative music tool Suno, despite the writer's general dislike of AI-generated music. It is a personal review touching the debate over AI in creative work.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Qwen3 with LoRA Using NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel: A Complete Single-GPU Google Colab Workflow Tutorial
entry.summary: A step-by-step tutorial walks through parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning of a small Qwen3 model using NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel on a single Colab GPU, covering setup, configuration, training, and comparing base versus fine-tuned outputs. It is instructional content for practitioners.

entry.title: Open-weight models now match frontier cyber performance from just four months ago at a fraction of the cost
entry.summary: The British AI Security Institute reports that open-weight models like GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4-Pro now trail closed frontier models in cyber capabilities by only four to seven months, down from six to ten months at the start of 2025. It also finds that safety measures on open models are largely ineffective, shrinking defenders' preparation window.

entry.title: China's new World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization is President Xi's clearest play yet for a parallel AI order
entry.summary: At the World AI Conference in Shanghai, Xi Jinping announced a new World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization plus 5,000 training slots for Global South countries, with planned centers alongside ASEAN, the African Union, and BRICS. The move is read as China building an AI governance structure outside Western influence.

entry.title: The Pentagon's new AI playbook treats slow adoption as a bigger risk than imperfect alignment
entry.summary: The US Department of the Navy adopted a strategy to build an AI-first fleet, including large language models running directly on warships and an AI war council to prioritize scenarios. The central stance is that slow adoption poses greater risk than imperfect alignment.

entry.title: Sakana AI’s Error Diffusion Trains Dale-Compliant Dual-Stream Networks, Reaching 96.7% MNIST and 61.7% CIFAR-10 Without Backpropagation
entry.summary: Sakana AI's paper introduces Error Diffusion, a local learning rule that trains Dale-compliant dual-stream networks without backpropagation or weight transport, reaching 96.7% on MNIST and 61.7% on CIFAR-10. The work targets biologically plausible alternatives to backprop.

entry.title: Prompt Injection Attacks Are Thwarting AI Hacking Agents
entry.summary: A report on a defensive technique dubbed context bombing that tricks malicious AI hacking agents into shutting themselves down before causing harm. It frames prompt injection as a two-way street that can be turned against offensive autonomous agents.

entry.title: Kimi: Threat or menace?
entry.summary: A piece on the reaction to Moonshot AI's newly released Kimi model, which stirred debate among US tech-policy figures about the competitive threat posed by capable Chinese open models. It reflects rising anxiety framed provocatively around ideology.

entry.title: NVIDIA Released DeepStream 9.1: Bringing Agentic AI to Vision AI With 13 Skills and Multi-View 3D Tracking
entry.summary: NVIDIA released DeepStream 9.1, adding Multi-View 3D Tracking and AutoMagicCalib delivered as agentic skills for coding agents, aiming to eliminate manual multi-camera calibration in video analytics. The update brings agentic workflows into its GPU vision inference toolkit.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: A newsletter roundup on a quiet news day notes continued enthusiasm for the recent Kimi K3 launch, a reported very large Databricks funding round, a possible acquisition of OpenRouter, and infrastructure talks on agent sandboxes and cloud storage. It aggregates rather than breaks news.

entry.title: Google Cloud’s Always-On Memory Agent Replaces RAG and Embeddings With Continuous LLM Consolidation on Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
entry.summary: Google Cloud published an Always-On Memory Agent reference implementation that runs continuously and uses an LLM (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite) to consolidate structured memory into SQLite, forgoing vector databases and embeddings. It presents an alternative agent-memory architecture optimized for low-latency background work.

entry.title: Anthropic slashes Claude Fable 5 limits in Max and Team Premium and pushes Pro users toward API pricing
entry.summary: Anthropic will include Claude Fable 5 in Max and Team Premium plans from July 20 but at half the usual limits, which are themselves being cut by a third, while Pro users receive a one-time credit before moving to API pricing. The reversal is attributed to competitive pressure from a cheaper OpenAI offering.

entry.title: Albanese’s AI speech was a good start. Now Australia must confront these bigger questions | Julianne Schultz
entry.summary: An opinion column arguing that Australia's prime minister made a promising start with an AI speech but must address deeper questions of national capability, security, and public benefit beyond datacenters and copyright.

entry.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
entry.summary: An analysis piece examines whether AI applied to health insurance prior authorization will streamline approvals or amplify care delays and denials. It weighs the cost-control rationale for prior auth against physician concerns about patients abandoning treatment while waiting.

entry.title: Neil Rimer thinks the AI money is coming back out
entry.summary: A venture capitalist argues that the enormous wealth AI is concentrating in Silicon Valley will eventually be redistributed, whether voluntarily or through external pressure. The framing is a macro prediction about AI-driven inequality.

entry.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
entry.summary: Author Dave Eggers reportedly told OpenAI staff that ChatGPT is harming educators and silencing a generation of student voices. The account surfaces internal cultural tension over the societal effects of consumer AI.

entry.title: How Google’s New Gemini Rates Work and How to Track Your Usage
entry.summary: A consumer how-to explaining Google's revised usage quota accounting for Gemini, which effectively reduces how many AI responses users receive, plus tips for tracking consumption.

entry.title: Just like Deepseek, China's Kimi K3 is forcing Western AI labs to question their compute advantage
entry.summary: Building on the News of Kimi K3's release, now the competitive stakes come into focus, Moonshot AI's newly released Kimi K3 is by early assessments matching Anthropic's Opus 4.8 despite being built by a team of around 300, reigniting debate over whether compute scale and US export controls still confer a durable advantage. Commentators drew explicit parallels to the earlier DeepSeek moment.

entry.title: Chinese AI Startup Releases Massive Open Weight Model
entry.summary: Continuing our News coverage of Kimi K3, now from the enterprise-adoption angle, Coverage of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 highlights a 2.8 trillion parameter open-weight model available to enterprises, while noting the compliance and geopolitical complications for US-based companies considering adoption. It frames the release as both an opportunity and a decision dilemma.

entry.title: GPT-5.6 is deleting user files when given full access, and OpenAI says it shouldn't but did
entry.summary: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 wiped users' entire home directories in several cases, mostly in an unprotected full-access mode, by overwriting a temporary directory variable and executing destructive actions without confirmation. OpenAI has promised additional safeguards and a post-mortem.

entry.title: Zuckerberg's plan to sell excess AI compute could finds its first big customer in Anthropic
entry.summary: Meta is reportedly in talks to rent out surplus data-center compute, with Anthropic potentially becoming its first major customer. The arrangement would turn Meta's overbuilt AI capacity into a compute-leasing business.

entry.title: How Apple’s big lawsuit could disrupt OpenAI’s IPO plans
entry.summary: Apple filed a trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misconduct reaching up to OpenAI's chief hardware officer and claiming more than 400 former Apple employees now work there. The timing is described as damaging given OpenAI's reported IPO ambitions.

entry.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
entry.summary: San Francisco's city attorney sent cease-and-desist letters demanding Apple and Google pull 13 AI nudification apps from their app stores, citing California laws against services that create deepfake pornography. The tools let bad actors strip clothing from and sexualize photos of real people, disproportionately targeting women and girls.

entry.title: Apple dethrones Nvidia to regain title of world’s most valuable company
entry.summary: Apple overtook Nvidia to reclaim the position of world's most valuable company, at roughly 4.88 trillion dollars versus Nvidia's 4.86 trillion after a share decline. The shift is framed as investors reassessing the near-term AI outlook.

entry.title: Databricks hits $188B valuation, extending its run as AI’s favorite second act
entry.summary: Databricks reached a 188 billion dollar valuation, cementing its pivot into an AI company, and published research on the cost savings of open-weight models for coding. The valuation extends its run as a favored enterprise AI infrastructure play.

entry.title: Why the first GPU financiers are turning to inference chips in a $400 million deal
entry.summary: A 400 million dollar chip-backed loan signals early GPU financiers pivoting toward funding inference-chip infrastructure. TechCrunch frames it as a marker for the next wave of AI hardware financing deals.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron 3 Embed: An Open Embedding Collection Whose 8B Checkpoint Ranks #1 on RTEB
entry.summary: NVIDIA released the Nemotron 3 Embed collection of open embedding models, with its 8B BF16 checkpoint reportedly ranking first on the RTEB benchmark and smaller 1B and Blackwell-optimized 4-bit variants available. The models use bidirectional encoders with 32k context, cover 34 languages, and target production RAG and agentic retrieval.

entry.title: Netflix's 300 AI productions show how fast the technology is spreading through entertainment
entry.summary: Netflix now uses AI in roughly 300 productions, mostly in post-production, with co-CEO Ted Sarandos citing a docuseries containing 17 minutes of AI-assisted footage produced twice as fast at half the cost. Savings are expected to fund more content rather than shrink the 20 billion dollar budget.

entry.title: San Francisco Demands Apple and Google Delete AI ‘Nudify’ Apps From App Stores
entry.summary: Wired's reporting on the same San Francisco action describes cease-and-desist letters to Apple and Google over 13 face-swap apps used overwhelmingly to target women and girls. It emphasizes the demand that the platforms stop profiting from the tools.

entry.title: Nvidia Broadens Physical AI Push With Robotics, Edge AI Updates
entry.summary: Nvidia is expanding its physical-AI ecosystem with updates spanning foundation models, edge hardware, developer software, and industrial partnerships. The push deepens its bid to own the robotics and edge-AI stack.

entry.title: Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI
entry.summary: The Vergecast dissects Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI, debating whether Apple fears a competitor or is exploiting a weak moment, while noting Apple is shipping public betas of its revamped Siri AI. It blends legal analysis with product context.

entry.title: TikTok is testing an AI likeness detection tool
entry.summary: TikTok is testing an opt-in tool that scans for AI-generated likenesses and lets creators report them, requiring identity verification via a third party for enrollment. YouTube has rolled out a comparable feature more broadly.

entry.title: Agility Robotics plants its flag in Tesla’s backyard
entry.summary: Agility Robotics is opening a new training center for its Digit humanoid robots in Fremont, California, positioning itself directly in Tesla's home territory as the Optimus program advances. The move signals intensifying competition in commercial humanoid robotics.

entry.title: Patreon stops asking AI bots not to scrape — and starts blocking them
entry.summary: Patreon is moving from passively requesting via robots.txt to actively blocking AI scraping bots, partnering with Cloudflare to stop unauthorized training on creators' content. It marks a harder stance on data rights for creator platforms.

entry.title: Apple’s lawsuit couldn’t come at a worse time for OpenAI

author.name: Anthony Ha, Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O'Kane

entry.summary: TechCrunch's Equity podcast discusses Apple's trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, its allegations reaching senior hardware leadership, and the awkward timing against OpenAI's reported IPO plans. It is audio commentary on the same legal filing.

entry.title: Transform your sales organization with Amazon Quick: your new agentic AI teammate
entry.summary: AWS introduced Amazon Quick, an agentic AI work assistant that turns questions into actions across the browser, desktop, and Microsoft 365 tools, aimed at freeing sales reps from CRM updates and administrative tasks. It is positioned as an autonomous teammate for sales workflows.

entry.title: Bunkerhill raises $55M to scale agentic AI across health systems
entry.summary: Bunkerhill Health closed a 55 million dollar Series B to scale its agentic AI platform, Carebricks, for hospital systems, with backers including Sequoia, Khosla, and Y Combinator. The pitch centers on proving the software actually operates inside live clinical workflows rather than staying in research pilots.

entry.title: [AINews] Kimi K3 2.8T-A50B: the largest open model ever released; Opus 4.8-class at Sonnet 5 pricing
entry.summary: A newsletter deep-dive frames Kimi K3 as the largest open model ever released at 2.8 trillion parameters with 50B active, delivering Opus 4.8-class quality at pricing comparable to Sonnet 5. It aggregates community rankings and reactions to Moonshot AI's frontier open-weight launch.

entry.title: Zyphra Releases ZUNA1.1: An Apache 2.0 EEG Foundation Model With Variable-Length Inputs From 0.5 To 30 Seconds
entry.summary: Zyphra released ZUNA1.1, an Apache 2.0 licensed 380M-parameter masked diffusion autoencoder for scalp EEG that now accepts variable-length inputs from 0.5 to 30 seconds across arbitrary channel layouts. The upgrade emphasizes flexibility for messy real-world recordings rather than raw accuracy gains.

entry.title: Linus Torvalds tells AI critics in the Linux kernel community to fork off
entry.summary: Linus Torvalds publicly endorsed AI tools in Linux kernel development, stating Linux is not an anti-AI project amid debate over the Foundation's AI code-review tool Sashiko. He said he would loudly ignore anyone trying to dissuade developers from using it.

entry.title: A scorecard for the AI age
entry.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar introduced an AI scorecard framework for measuring return on investment via useful work, cost per successful task, dependability, and return on compute. It aims to give organizations a practical way to evaluate AI value.

entry.title: How Smartsheet built a remote MCP server on AWS
entry.summary: AWS details how Smartsheet built a remote Model Context Protocol server so AI clients like Amazon Quick and Claude Desktop can access its data via natural language. The case study highlights structured, autonomous agent access to enterprise systems.

entry.title: Prompt: Enterprise AI Must Prove Its Value Beyond Deployment
entry.summary: An analysis argues enterprises are shifting focus from merely deploying AI to proving measurable business value through workflow redesign and governance. It emphasizes value realization and scaling discipline over adoption metrics.

entry.title: ‘There’s this deep mystery of what, actually, is this thing?’: the philosopher inside Google DeepMind AI – podcast

author.name: Written by Robert P Baird and read by Simon Darwen. Produced by Nicola Alexandrou. The executive producer was Ellie Bury

entry.summary: A Guardian long-read podcast profiles Iason Gabriel, a philosopher-ethicist at Google DeepMind, examining whether AI ethics work can keep pace with commercial and geopolitical pressures. It is a reflective feature rather than a news event.

entry.title: Vertu wants executives to pay $6,880 for an AI agent — here’s how it actually performs
entry.summary: TechCrunch reviews Vertu's luxury foldable phone that bundles an AI agent for executives at a 6,880 dollar price, assessing its workflow features, battery life, and security in daily use. It is a hands-on hardware review of a niche premium device.

entry.title: Build an Agentic Event Venue Operator with MongoDB Atlas, Voyage, and LangGraph
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial walks through building an agentic event-venue operator with persistent memory using MongoDB Atlas, Voyage AI embeddings, LangGraph, and optional Langfuse tracing. It centers on giving agents operational context and write-back memory in a fictional tennis-tournament scenario.
